Ok, I've managed to avoid the crashes on ios devices by modifying the source code of the bullet extension to use the btTransform class instead of the Matrix4 class and recompile the whole thing. Note that this is simply a workaround that I just wanted to try before really fixing the bug properly. The results are interesting ... The code runs on all devices without crashes, however, ios devices still show strange behaviour. The code works on all other (non-ios) devices though. 

I have posted on the libgdx forum 3 videos showing the results. http://www.badlogicgames.com/forum/viewtopic.php?f=11&t=12276&p=55074#

Is there anyone who can explain the behaviour when running on the ipad? If someone can point me to the right direction I can maybe fix this issue, which would be nice since this bug is a bit of a gamebreaker for bullet-users.

I'm also still interested to know whether someone else managed to get bullet working properly on a real ios device or whether anyone else is struggling with this issue.

Hmm yes, I also saw the video and I’m also not sure what exactly happened. The video is quite old so I presume an update to the code broke something small. I’m quite sure that the problem can easily be resolved with minor code changes, but the question is always what to change … Anyways, here are some pointers to get you started.
- 1. You must know that the bug is located in cpp territory, not java. Libgdx calls native bullet code, which is cpp, through the “java native interface” (JNI). If you don’t know what JNI is, google it. Also check http://www3.ntu.edu.sg/home/ehchua/programming/java/JavaNativeInterface.html for more information regarding JNI. If everything looks like chinees in the beginning, don’t worry, it was the same for me. I just know JNI sinds a couple of months ago. Just try to get a basic understanding, that is all.
- 1. You must be able to compile the libgdx library. This is very simple. Download the master zip at https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx and follow https://code.google.com/p/libgdx/wiki/SourceBuilding. On my machine, mac os x (Hackintosh), I simply had to install Ant, browse to the main libgdx source folder (containing build.xml) and type “ant” in the terminal. As the website describes, this will NOT build the native libraries (the ones written in cpp code), this must be done separately. You do not need to compile the libgdx lib per se to fix the bug, but managing to do this, will help with the next step.
- 1. Build the bullet extension library for ios. Look in the folder $libgdxSource/extensions/gdx-bullet/jni
     There you will again find a build.xml file. In this file you define what version of the bullet-extension you want to build (Windows, mac, iOS, …). Modify it to only build the version for iOS. Once this is done, open a terminal, browse to the folder with the aforementioned build.xml, and type ant. This should compile, link and create the file libgdx-bullet.a, which can be found in $libgdxSource/extensions/gdx-bullet/libs/ios32. 
- 1. Modify the JNI code. As indicated by Xoppa, the bug is probably in the mapping from the bullet (btVector3, btQuaternion, btMatrix3x3, btTransform) to the libgdx (Vector3, Quaternion, Matrix3, Matrix4) datatypes (see https://code.google.com/p/libgdx/wiki/PhysicsBullet common classes). 

To start debugging, the best thing to do is to make a very simple bullet-enabled libgdx project. Make sure it compiles AND runs on the iOS device. Then, Make it deliberately crash calling the method btRigidBody.getWorldTransform(). Make sure it crashes on the iOS device. Next, go to $libgdxSource/extensions/gdx-bullet/jni/swig-src/collision and open collision_wrap.cpp. Search for the function 

SWIGEXPORT jlong JNICALL Java_com_badlogic_gdx_physics_bullet_collision_CollisionJNI_btCollisionObject_1getWorldTransform_1_1SWIG_10(JNIEnv *jenv, jclass jcls, jlong jarg1, jobject jarg1_)

This function contains the JNI code when calling btRigidBody.getWorldTransform(). I noticed that when commenting the following two lines

//jresult = gdx_getReturnMatrix4(jenv);
//gdx_setMatrix4FrombtTransform(jenv, jresult, result);

The program will not crash anymore, meaning the bug is somewhere in “gdx_getReturnMatrix4” or “gdx_setMatrix4FrombtTransform”. I modified this function to return an object of type btTransform instead of Matrix4, which avoids calling the previously mentioned functions. The code worked on all systems, except for real iOS devices. You can check the videos on the libgx forum (for the link, see my previous posts). Though the crashes did disappeared, there was still some strange behaviour on real iOS devices, which I cannot explain at all. 

The best thing to do in my opinion is to fix the functions responsible for mapping the bullet and libgdx datatypes (gdx_getReturnMatrix4, gdx_setMatrix4FrombtTransform,…). Maybe this will fix the crashes without any side effect. A small tip, use githubs search functionality for searching the broken functions. (https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/search?q=gdx_getReturnMatrix4&ref=cmdform).

Also make sure to recompile the library every time you wish to check your changes in the JNI code. I also used a simple printf during debugging to test whether my test program was using the updated libgdx-bullet.a file. Also don’t forget to replace lingdx-bullet.a in your test-project.

If you have more questions or are facing difficulties with something, feel free to ask. 

Good luck!

regards,
Leon
